local33-u4cacf50dc770e1b3a3-1.locator: Article 41. Control and supervision of the activities of local self-government bodies and local self-government officials

local33-ub633d94b176ede57a6-1.text: 18. The period for providing information may be shortened where violations of the legislation of the Russian Federation causing emergencies, threatening citizens’ lives and health or entailing mass violations of citizens’ rights have been established.
local33-ub633d94b176ede57a6-1.locator: Article 41. Control and supervision of the activities of local self-government bodies and local self-government officials

local33-u1a9bdacfaa105c8e38-1.text: 19. Local self-government bodies and officials may decline to provide information requested by state control (supervision) bodies if it was provided previously, officially published in the mass media or posted on the official website of the local self-government body on the Internet information and telecommunications network. In their reply to the request, the local self-government body or official shall indicate the source where the information was officially published or posted.
local33-u1a9bdacfaa105c8e38-1.locator: Article 41. Control and supervision of the activities of local self-government bodies and local self-government officials

local33-u5fc8513ba7c570b5a7-1.text: 20. When issuing orders to remedy identified violations and setting deadlines for compliance, state control (supervision) bodies must take into account the need for local self-government bodies to comply with the requirements and procedures established by the legislation of the Russian Federation.
local33-u5fc8513ba7c570b5a7-1.locator: Article 41. Control and supervision of the activities of local self-government bodies and local self-government officials

local33-u10ac756ec555954503-1.text: 21. This Article does not apply where federal laws establish another procedure for organizing and conducting control (supervision) over the activities of local self-government bodies and officials, or to control (supervision) measures conducted by officials of federal security service bodies.
local33-u10ac756ec555954503-1.locator: Article 41. Control and supervision of the activities of local self-government bodies and local self-government officials

local33-u43c8e39da0d3d09a1f-1.text: Chapter 5. Direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government
local33-u43c8e39da0d3d09a1f-1.locator: Chapter 5. Direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-u2955347842260be837-1.text: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government
local33-u2955347842260be837-1.locator: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-ufcbf709cf1a48dd067-1.text: 1. The forms in which the population directly exercises local self-government include:
local33-ufcbf709cf1a48dd067-1.locator: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-u1d47e1d6c5a11d4bb6-1.locator: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-u682f9d7f329f98696f-1.locator: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-ubed7ab91256528b91c-1.locator: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-ue89fce4f44aa91f214-1.text: 2. Forms of the population’s participation in the exercise of local self-government include:
local33-ue89fce4f44aa91f214-1.locator: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-ubcedde55ee40f13c95-1.locator: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-u4543522e2c8931c080-1.locator: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-ufcc28eaf5b830e2245-1.locator: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-u400b60bfcdcbe10c72-1.locator: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-u525ecd23272b71a96d-1.locator: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-uebac96c162e831c44d-1.locator: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-u66d26632782dc6a50d-1.text: 3. In addition to the forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation in its exercise provided for by this Federal Law, citizens may participate in local self-government in other forms that do not conflict with the Constitution of the Russian Federation, this Federal Law, other federal laws or laws of constituent entities of the Russian Federation.
local33-u66d26632782dc6a50d-1.locator: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-u5f5944f064e2aabb70-1.text: 4. Direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation in its exercise are based on the principles of legality and voluntariness.
local33-u5f5944f064e2aabb70-1.locator: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-u7bae4bcb824437daf3-1.text: 5. Public authorities and their officials must assist the population in directly exercising local self-government and participating in its exercise.
local33-u7bae4bcb824437daf3-1.locator: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-u32abda7a93d6345ad7-1.text: 6. Local self-government bodies of urban okrugs and municipal okrugs may, in accordance with municipal charters, decide to involve citizens on a voluntary basis in work of social significance to the urban or municipal okrug (including duty shifts) in order to resolve matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life.
local33-u32abda7a93d6345ad7-1.locator: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-uff86d7a2e879f6b68f-1.text: 7. Only work that does not require special professional training may be classified as work of social significance.
local33-uff86d7a2e879f6b68f-1.locator: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-ue3069ffa4be498e307-1.text: 8. Adult residents of urban okrugs and municipal okrugs who are capable of work may be involved in work of social significance, without remuneration and outside their main working or study hours, no more than once every three months. Such work may not last for more than four consecutive hours.
local33-ue3069ffa4be498e307-1.locator: Article 42. Forms of direct exercise of local self-government by the population and participation of the population in the exercise of local self-government

local33-u2d35a481d2989c19de-1.text: 1. A local referendum is held for the population to decide directly on matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life.

local33-u8773ec220402e584f4-1.text: 2. A federal law, the constitution (charter) or a law of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation, or the municipal charter may determine matters that must be submitted to a local referendum.

local33-ub8b9b0ac4a1f3798d3-1.text: 3. A local referendum is held throughout the territory of the municipality.

local33-uaec3704e93679edcc9-1.text: 4. A decision to call a local referendum is adopted by the municipal representative body:

local33-u4e3731895962034339-1.text: 1) at the initiative of citizens of the Russian Federation entitled to participate in the local referendum;

local33-ueb5c576a6da64a4325-1.text: 2) at the initiative of electoral associations or other public associations whose charters provide for participation in elections and/or referendums and which are registered in accordance with the procedure and within the time limits established by federal law;

local33-u348e315c32c866833e-1.text: 3) at the joint initiative of the municipal representative body and the head of the local administration.

local33-u3d7f283d24e969d837-1.text: 5. Calling a local referendum at the initiative of citizens, electoral associations or other public associations referred to in point 2 of part 4 of this Article requires the collection of signatures in support of the initiative. The number of signatures is established by a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation and may not exceed 5 percent of the number of referendum participants registered in the municipality in accordance with federal law.

local33-ud3ca4ffaf43e5b6d45-1.text: 6. A referendum initiative proposed by citizens, electoral associations or other public associations referred to in point 2 of part 4 of this Article is formalized in accordance with the procedure established by federal law and a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation adopted in accordance with it.

local33-u1d7f65ea3d7f3cf1de-1.text: 7. A referendum initiative proposed jointly by the municipal representative body and the head of the local administration is formalized by legal acts of the representative body and the head of the local administration.

local33-u6bac7de4450e6f1f50-1.text: 8. The municipal representative body must call a local referendum within 30 days after receiving the documents on the basis of which the referendum is to be called.

local33-ue68afefb20dd55c3a0-1.text: 9. If the municipal representative body fails to call a local referendum within the established time limits, the referendum is called by a court upon an application by citizens, electoral associations, the head of the municipality, state authorities of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation or a prosecutor. A local referendum called by a court is organized by the relevant referendum commission, and support for its conduct is provided by an executive body of the constituent entity or another body designated by the court to ensure the conduct of the referendum.

local33-u3a610d846c5dcae8ee-1.text: 10. Citizens of the Russian Federation whose place of residence is within the municipality’s boundaries have the right to participate in a local referendum. Citizens of the Russian Federation participate in a local referendum on the basis of universal, equal and direct expression of will by secret ballot.

local33-u71cc3150ba22e0b57d-1.text: 11. The voting results and the decision adopted at a local referendum must be officially published.

local33-u2b816f8ced7cb3628d-1.text: 12. A decision adopted at a local referendum is binding throughout the municipality and does not require approval by any public authorities or their officials.

local33-u08d9d4248d19fe5f23-1.text: 13. Local self-government bodies ensure implementation of the decision adopted at a local referendum in accordance with the division of powers among them determined by the municipal charter.

local33-u95a394ffd48d0d1f60-1.text: 14. A decision to hold a local referendum and a decision adopted at a local referendum may be challenged in court by citizens, local self-government bodies, a prosecutor or state authorities authorized by federal law.

local33-u7630f91e7d03c314dc-1.text: 15. Guarantees of citizens’ rights to participate in a local referendum and the procedure for preparing and conducting it are established by federal law and laws of constituent entities of the Russian Federation adopted in accordance with it.

local33-u23894c361d685eef77-1.text: 1. Municipal elections are held to elect deputies, the head of the municipality and other persons holding municipal offices in accordance with the municipal charter, on the basis of universal, equal and direct suffrage by secret ballot.

local33-u2a2f1595169bf71f8f-1.text: 2. Municipal elections are called by the municipal representative body within the time limits provided for by the municipal charter. In the cases established by federal law, municipal elections are called by the relevant election commission or a court.

local33-u3cbd7425efc3c13e42-1.text: 3. Guarantees of citizens’ electoral rights in municipal elections and the procedure for calling, preparing and conducting municipal elections, establishing vote totals and determining election results are established by federal law and laws of constituent entities of the Russian Federation adopted in accordance with it.

local33-u965ee341038ce17701-1.text: 4. A law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation, in accordance with this Federal Law and other federal laws, establishes the types of electoral systems that may be used in municipal elections and the procedure for their use.

local33-ufa631347b9aec4ead0-1.text: 5. In accordance with the types of electoral systems established by a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation, the municipal charter determines the electoral system used in municipal elections in that municipality. In this Article, an electoral system means the conditions for recognizing a candidate or candidates as elected, admitting lists of candidates to the allocation of deputy mandates, and the procedure for allocating mandates among lists of candidates and within those lists.

local33-u7f29a283615c600abb-1.text: 6. A law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation may, in accordance with this Federal Law and other federal laws, determine the conditions for using types of electoral systems in municipalities depending on the number of voters, the type of municipality and other circumstances.

local33-ufa1cc5e089cc098cc4-1.text: 7. Elections of deputies of representative bodies of urban okrugs and municipal okrugs having fewer than 15 deputies are held in single-member and/or multi-member constituencies.

local33-u5d4f61cd25cb68dcc0-1.text: 8. If, in a municipal representative body elected in municipal elections, some deputy mandates are distributed under electoral legislation among lists of candidates nominated by political parties (their regional branches or other structural subdivisions) in proportion to the number of votes received by each list, at least 10 deputy mandates must be distributed among those lists.

local33-ud686fab4aa143755b5-1.text: 9. The results of municipal elections must be officially published.

local33-ucb75dfd6f85f2d6d95-1.text: 1. In the cases provided for by this Federal Law, a citizens’ assembly may be held:

local33-u8e8b21f0851f1f54af-1.text: 1) in a settlement forming part of the municipality’s territory, on introducing and using citizens’ self-taxation funds in that settlement;

local33-ub90f2427ddb4bdd700-1.text: 2) in accordance with a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation, in part of the territory of a settlement forming part of the municipality’s territory, on introducing and using citizens’ self-taxation funds in that part of the settlement;

local33-u9f14956cbd72fa2a10-1.text: 3) throughout the municipality or in part of its territory, to ascertain citizens’ opinions on support for an initiative project.

local33-uffa168766112de4db4-1.text: 2. In the cases provided for by the legislation of the Russian Federation on municipal service, a citizens’ assembly may be held in a rural settlement to nominate candidates for a competition commission when a competition to fill a municipal service position is held.

local33-u13ec95611e6de4e7ba-1.text: 3. A citizens’ assembly may be convened by the head of the municipality or by the municipal representative body, including at the initiative of a group of at least 10 residents of the relevant part of the settlement.

local33-ucf572fede2357380fe-1.text: 4. The head of the municipality ensures that the citizens’ assembly is held.

local33-udefde5666559038ea2-1.text: 5. The procedure for organizing and holding a citizens’ assembly is determined by the municipal charter and must provide for advance notification of municipal residents of the assembly’s time and place, advance access to the draft municipal legal act and materials on matters submitted for decision by the assembly, and other measures ensuring municipal residents’ participation in the assembly.

local33-u03b064074a1b7fee0d-1.text: 6. The criteria for determining the boundaries of a part of a settlement within the municipality where a citizens’ assembly may be held on introducing and using citizens’ self-taxation funds are established by a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation.

local33-u6e991b97ce5b0c2732-1.text: 7. A citizens’ assembly is quorate if more than half of the residents of the settlement (or part of its territory) who have voting rights participate.

local33-uaf9d426f54de698ab6-1.text: 8. If a settlement cannot accommodate the simultaneous joint presence of more than half of its residents who have voting rights, the citizens’ assembly is held in stages in accordance with the charter of the municipality that includes the settlement, within a period not exceeding one month after the decision to hold the assembly. Persons who have already participated in the assembly do not take part in voting at subsequent stages.

local33-u412231720d26d8d875-1.text: 9. A decision of a citizens’ assembly is considered adopted if more than half of the assembly’s participants vote in favor.

local33-u510fdc753f08e7ccf1-1.text: 10. Local self-government bodies and officials ensure implementation of decisions adopted at a citizens’ assembly in accordance with the division of powers among them determined by the municipal charter.

local33-u7857f583ebab9baed2-1.text: 11. Decisions adopted at a citizens’ assembly must be officially published.

local33-ue3a37b2b3cb8c62da7-1.text: 1. A citizens’ survey may be conducted throughout a municipality or in part of its territory to ascertain public opinion when local self-government bodies and officials take decisions in exercising powers to resolve matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life, and when state authorities of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation take decisions in exercising powers concerning the establishment of general principles for the organization of local self-government.

local33-u8378909aeee62fc4f6-1.text: 2. Residents of the municipality who have voting rights are entitled to participate in a citizens’ survey.

local33-u36a9afebc0680265c3-1.text: 3. Residents aged eighteen or over of the municipality or part of it in which an initiative project is proposed to be implemented may participate in a survey to ascertain citizens’ opinions on support for that initiative project.

local33-u5f312fdea4ed498a8e-1.text: 4. A citizens’ survey is conducted at the initiative of:

local33-u4adc695f52b1504191-1.text: 1) the municipal representative body, the head of the municipality or the head of the local administration;

local33-u71a0cee462c7e99a03-1.text: 2) state authorities of constituent entities of the Russian Federation;

local33-u4ac0c6cf320e032f4f-1.text: 3) residents of the municipality or part of it in which an initiative project is proposed to be implemented, to ascertain citizens’ opinions on support for that initiative project.

local33-u56cf75235cd719cffe-1.text: 5. The procedure for calling and conducting a citizens’ survey is determined by regulatory legal acts of the municipal representative body in accordance with a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation.

local33-u518653959ca67cb631-1.text: 6. The municipal representative body must decide to call a citizens’ survey within three months after receipt of a survey initiative provided for in part 4 of this Article.

local33-u32f298137671abb3f0-1.text: 7. The decision of the municipal representative body to call a citizens’ survey establishes:

local33-u3db34ea41e70b2917d-1.text: 1) the date and duration of the survey;

local33-ue078da943e591286a6-1.text: 2) the wording of the question or questions put in the survey;

local33-u8a3bb9430b891ee431-1.text: 5) the minimum number of municipal residents participating in the survey;

local33-ua905d6f1a97f58f301-1.text: 6) the procedure for identifying survey participants if the survey is conducted using the municipality’s official website on the Internet information and telecommunications network.

local33-u8d3447ccd802633f96-1.text: 8. Municipal residents must be informed of the citizens’ survey by the authorized local self-government body or official at least 10 days before it is conducted.

local33-uccae87d9df55fcfb07-1.text: 9. The municipality’s official website on the Internet information and telecommunications network may be used to conduct a citizens’ survey.

local33-ubec2533541c24111e2-1.text: 10. Activities related to preparing and conducting a citizens’ survey are financed:

local33-u29d6003dc62aad50aa-1.text: 1) from the local budget where the survey is conducted at the initiative of local self-government bodies or municipal residents;

local33-uc2be29bd9bf1440903-1.text: 2) from the budget of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation where the survey is conducted at the initiative of state authorities of that constituent entity.

local33-u90adf3932def4ea02a-1.text: 11. The survey results are advisory in nature.

local33-u4ad491367039312d8d-1.text: 12. The survey results must be made public.

local33-u65c3e9e37f942b6b44-1.text: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions
local33-u65c3e9e37f942b6b44-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-u2d237e6568d9acfaa5-1.text: 1. Public hearings may be held throughout the municipality to discuss draft municipal legal acts on matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life, with the participation of municipal residents.
local33-u2d237e6568d9acfaa5-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-ubd53eef2a50e89008e-1.text: 2. The following must be submitted to public hearings:
local33-ubd53eef2a50e89008e-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-u382ac9d49be804e5d7-1.text: 1) the draft municipal charter and a draft municipal regulatory legal act amending or supplementing that charter, except where amendments to the charter exactly reproduce provisions of the Constitution of the Russian Federation, federal laws, or the constitution (charter) or laws of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation in order to bring the charter into conformity with those regulatory legal acts;
local33-u382ac9d49be804e5d7-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-u0a9c5f0e0985b2bce5-1.text: 2) the draft local budget and the report on its execution;
local33-u0a9c5f0e0985b2bce5-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-u95542c4fc0fe1414f9-1.text: 3) matters concerning transformation of the municipality.
local33-u95542c4fc0fe1414f9-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-uee6f9d4fa34a42ba6d-1.text: 3. Municipal residents aged eighteen or over have the right to participate in public hearings.
local33-uee6f9d4fa34a42ba6d-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-ub09e5e6c377e9aa619-1.text: 4. Public hearings are held at the initiative of:
local33-ub09e5e6c377e9aa619-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-u77c57fdbb6f66f87b5-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-u1f37fe78dfbc3f3385-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-u7fc2e39dc69187c522-1.text: 3) the head of the local administration;
local33-u7fc2e39dc69187c522-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-ued38d05dab120e1937-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-ua61197e5ef31b6ae51-1.text: 5. The procedure for calling and conducting public hearings is determined by regulatory legal acts of the municipal representative body in accordance with a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation.
local33-ua61197e5ef31b6ae51-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-u5124b4577e7a943799-1.text: 6. The procedure for public hearings must provide for notification of municipal residents of the time and place of the hearings and access to the draft municipal legal act, including by posting it on the official website of the local self-government body on the Internet information and telecommunications network, at least 10 days before the hearings; opportunities for residents to submit comments and proposals on the draft submitted for discussion, including through that official website; and other measures ensuring municipal residents’ participation in public hearings.
local33-u5124b4577e7a943799-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-u81e1248ab6d672ca65-1.text: 7. Regulatory legal acts of the municipal representative body may provide that, to post the materials and information specified in part 6 of this Article, enable municipal residents to submit comments and proposals on a draft municipal legal act, and allow them to participate in public hearings, while complying with the requirement to use the local self-government body’s official website on the Internet information and telecommunications network for those purposes, the federal state information system “Unified Portal of State and Municipal Services (Functions)” may be used. The procedure for using that system for the purposes of this Article is established by the Government of the Russian Federation.
local33-u81e1248ab6d672ca65-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-ucad0df6db422aaa174-1.text: 8. Public hearings held at the initiative of municipal residents or the municipal representative body are called by the representative body; public hearings held at the initiative of the head of the municipality or the head of the local administration are called by the head of the municipality.
local33-ucad0df6db422aaa174-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-u8e4f172d2d9f8d48ba-1.text: 9. The municipal representative body or the head of the municipality must decide to call public hearings within 10 days after receiving an initiative provided for in part 4 of this Article.
local33-u8e4f172d2d9f8d48ba-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-ub34570d37ae493bdbe-1.text: 10. Public hearings or public discussions are held in accordance with urban development legislation on draft master plans; draft land use and development rules; draft territorial layout plans; draft territorial land parcel boundary plans; draft territorial improvement and upkeep rules; drafts amending any of those approved documents; draft decisions granting permission for a conditionally permitted use of a land plot or capital construction facility; draft decisions permitting deviations from the limiting parameters of permitted construction or reconstruction of capital construction facilities; and changes from one permitted use of land plots or capital construction facilities to another in the absence of approved land use and development rules.
local33-ub34570d37ae493bdbe-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-u60992b50bf29290afa-1.text: 11. The municipal representative body must consider the results of public hearings and public discussions when considering draft municipal legal acts.
local33-u60992b50bf29290afa-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-ue8ddb7637c2f1b4a1e-1.text: 12. The results of public hearings and public discussions, including reasoned explanations of the decisions taken, must be made public.
local33-ue8ddb7637c2f1b4a1e-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-u99fad92c37bc088944-1.text: 13. The results of public hearings and public discussions are advisory in nature.
local33-u99fad92c37bc088944-1.locator: Article 47. Public hearings and public discussions

local33-ucbf760e80dbcc9028f-1.text: 1) to discuss matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life;

local33-ue0e5aa3608b133e980-1.text: 2) to inform the population about the activities of local self-government bodies and officials;

local33-u5f50e7c260043c653e-1.text: 3) throughout the municipality or in part of its territory, to ascertain citizens’ opinions on support for an initiative project;

local33-ue7aa2d64291787062e-1.text: 4) in a rural settlement, to nominate a candidate for rural settlement elder or to consider early termination of the elder’s powers;

local33-ua4246092c874602a36-1.text: 5) to exercise territorial public self-government in part of the municipality’s territory.

local33-ua4a2caa3e60897614c-1.text: 2. A citizens’ meeting is held at the initiative of the population, the municipal representative body or the head of the municipality, and also in the cases provided for by the charter of territorial public self-government.

local33-ufae2edda66855b2f54-1.text: 3. A citizens’ meeting held at the initiative of the municipal representative body or the head of the municipality is called by the representative body or the head of the municipality.

local33-u19efe9eca1c6d15e26-1.text: 4. A citizens’ meeting held at the initiative of the population is called by the municipal representative body in accordance with the procedure established by its regulatory legal act.

local33-u479e11f556edde1fed-1.text: 5. The procedure for calling and holding a citizens’ meeting, and its powers, are determined by this Federal Law, regulatory legal acts of the municipal representative body and the charter of territorial public self-government.

local33-uf74bec2f5f01f515f9-1.text: 6. The procedure for calling and holding citizens’ meetings provided for in points 1–4 of part 1 of this Article is determined by a regulatory legal act of the municipal representative body.

local33-u4692352642a5adeb4c-1.text: 7. The procedure for calling and holding a citizens’ meeting for the exercise of territorial public self-government is determined by the charter of territorial public self-government.

local33-u8ba936e17806308001-1.text: 8. Residents aged eighteen or over of the relevant territory may participate in a citizens’ meeting held throughout the municipality or in part of its territory to ascertain citizens’ opinions on support for an initiative project.

local33-u5f6266a89c70569c33-1.text: 9. A citizens’ meeting held in a rural settlement to nominate a candidate for rural settlement elder or to consider early termination of the elder’s powers may be attended by citizens of the Russian Federation who reside in that settlement and have the right to vote, and also, where municipal regulatory legal acts so provide in accordance with a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation, by citizens of the Russian Federation aged eighteen or over on the date of the meeting who own residential premises in that rural settlement.

local33-u855b7b9e68e8369f98-1.text: 10. A decision to nominate a candidate for rural settlement elder or to terminate the elder’s powers early is adopted by a majority of votes of the participants in the citizens’ meeting.

local33-ub9707bc3f72e073fb9-1.text: 11. A citizens’ meeting may adopt appeals to local self-government bodies and officials and elect persons authorized to represent the meeting in relations with those bodies and officials.

local33-u82d83dedb9e44ae181-1.text: 12. A citizens’ meeting held on matters relating to territorial public self-government adopts decisions on matters assigned to its competence by the charter of territorial public self-government.

local33-uab6784f7dcf3f7f37d-1.text: 13. Appeals adopted by a citizens’ meeting must be considered by the local self-government bodies and officials competent to resolve the matters raised, and a written reply must be sent.

local33-u0ad2a5935804e30f27-1.text: 14. The outcomes of a citizens’ meeting must be officially made public.

local33-u81d6bd2a72ac7c8d27-1.text: 1. An initiative project may be submitted to the local administration, including through a territorial body of the local administration, to implement measures of priority importance to residents of the municipality or part of it, addressing matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life or other matters that local self-government bodies are entitled to resolve.

local33-ud8dff06d8994117d89-1.text: 2. The procedure for determining the part of a municipality’s territory in which initiative projects may be implemented is established by a regulatory legal act of the municipal representative body.

local33-ud2ae6e0857dc988bea-1.text: 3. An initiative project may be proposed by an initiative group of at least 10 citizens aged eighteen or over who reside in the municipality concerned, territorial public self-government bodies, or a rural settlement elder (hereinafter, project initiators). The minimum size of an initiative group may be reduced by a regulatory legal act of the municipal representative body. A regulatory legal act of the municipal representative body may also grant the right to act as a project initiator to other persons conducting activities in the municipality concerned.

local33-u871a81b5be41cb37a0-1.text: 4. An initiative project must contain the following information:

local33-u18322a3ddf1731d0a2-1.text: 1) a description of the problem whose resolution is of priority importance to residents of the municipality or part of it;

local33-ub4ad95f2112ab383d7-1.text: 2) justification of the proposals for resolving that problem;

local33-uca6e0dcac66c5ffada-1.text: 3) a description of the expected outcome or outcomes of the initiative project;

local33-uf1438e91348cc3fca6-1.text: 4) a preliminary estimate of the expenditure necessary to implement the initiative project;

local33-u7d5efd60871eb92443-1.text: 5) the planned implementation timetable for the initiative project;

local33-u1420fc21e593074d72-1.text: 6) information on planned (possible) financial, property and/or labor contributions by interested persons to implementation of the project;

local33-u978bd697939dec9728-1.text: 7) the amount of local budget funds, if such funds are expected to be used to implement the initiative project, excluding the planned amount of initiative contributions;

local33-ue9eb7a70c8a839f594-1.text: 8) identification of the territory of the municipality or part of it within which the initiative project will be implemented, in accordance with the procedure established by a regulatory legal act of the municipal representative body;

local33-u41205782252e37a6dd-1.text: 9) other information provided for by a regulatory legal act of the municipal representative body.

local33-u211940a2f02b547a0b-1.text: 5. Before submission to the local administration, an initiative project must be considered at a citizens’ assembly or meeting, including a citizens’ meeting on the exercise of territorial public self-government in part of the municipality, to discuss the project, determine whether it meets the interests of residents of the municipality or part of it and whether its implementation is appropriate, and adopt a decision of the assembly or meeting supporting it. Several initiative projects may be considered at the same citizens’ assembly or meeting.

local33-u663848dba7d41c1f18-1.text: 6. In addition to the mandatory support for an initiative project provided for in part 5 of this Article, a regulatory legal act of the municipal representative body may provide for further ascertainment of citizens’ opinions on support for the project through a citizens’ survey and/or other means of ascertaining public opinion.

local33-uccf1ea9bdee1bba45c-1.text: 7. When submitting an initiative project to the local administration, project initiators attach the minutes of the citizens’ assembly or meeting and the results of further ascertainment of citizens’ opinions through a survey and/or other means, confirming support for the project by residents of the municipality or part of it.

local33-u75491226a1ce79b35c-1.text: 8. Information on submission of an initiative project to the local administration must be made public, including by posting on the municipality’s official website on the Internet information and telecommunications network, within three working days after submission. It must contain the information specified in part 4 of this Article and information about the project initiators. At the same time, citizens are informed of the opportunity to submit comments and proposals on the project to the local administration, with a submission period of at least five working days. Municipal residents aged eighteen or over may submit comments and proposals. In a rural settlement, the rural settlement elder may bring this information to citizens’ attention.

local33-ube69b6b731e191a46b-1.text: 9. The local administration must consider an initiative project within 30 days after its submission. Following consideration, the local administration adopts one of the following decisions:

local33-u28c8fe52dc9d1fded7-1.text: 1) support the initiative project and continue work on it within the budget appropriations provided for the relevant purposes by the local budget decision and/or in accordance with the procedure for preparing and considering the draft local budget (amending the local budget decision);

local33-u96fd978646155b0f05-1.text: 2) refuse to support the initiative project and return it to the project initiators, stating the reasons for refusal.

local33-ueaf043a564e2430f26-1.text: 10. The local administration decides to refuse support for an initiative project in one of the following cases:

local33-u168f5f32ac1c2e2be7-1.text: 1) failure to comply with the established procedure for submitting and considering the initiative project;

local33-u838a650e254f07b2dc-1.text: 2) the initiative project does not comply with federal laws and other regulatory legal acts of the Russian Federation, laws and other regulatory legal acts of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, or the municipal charter;

local33-u5c2a1d27afa42d8530-1.text: 3) the initiative project cannot be implemented because local self-government bodies lack the necessary powers and rights to exercise powers not assigned to local self-government bodies;

local33-ub71f584230612d44e4-1.text: 4) insufficient local budget funds from sources other than initiative contributions to implement the initiative project;

local33-u456f8384a5f8688d24-1.text: 5) the problem described in the initiative project can be resolved more effectively by another means;

local33-u9b2e83d074de888441-1.text: 6) the initiative project has been found not to have passed competitive selection.

local33-u2a24dd899faa5e45c3-1.text: 11. The local administration may, and in the case provided for in point 5 of part 10 of this Article must, propose that the project initiators jointly revise the initiative project, and recommend submitting it to the public authority competent to consider it.

local33-u8c59a097297175d279-1.text: 12. The procedure for proposing, submitting, discussing and considering initiative projects, and for their competitive selection, is established by the municipal representative body.

local33-ue4b25b6de91ce563d1-1.text: 13. For initiative projects proposed to obtain financial support through interbudgetary transfers from the budget of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation, the required contents of projects, the procedure for considering them, including grounds for refusing support, and the procedure and criteria for their competitive selection are established in accordance with a law and/or other regulatory legal act of the constituent entity. In that case, the requirements of parts 4, 9–12, 14 and 15 of this Article do not apply.

local33-uedfcf7df48bff63436-1.text: 14. If several initiative projects are submitted to the local administration, including projects describing priority problems of similar substance, the local administration organizes competitive selection and informs the project initiators.

local33-u85696c57777c4d5e06-1.text: 15. Competitive selection of initiative projects is entrusted to a collegial body (commission), whose formation and operating procedures are determined by a regulatory legal act of the municipal representative body. The local administration forms the membership of the collegial body (commission). Half of its total membership must be appointed on the basis of proposals from the municipal representative body. During competitive selection, project initiators and their representatives must be given the opportunity to participate in the collegial body’s (commission’s) consideration of initiative projects and to present their positions on them.

local33-u2b1c21515d1a799adb-1.text: 16. Project initiators, other citizens residing in the relevant municipality and authorized by a citizens’ assembly or meeting, and other persons specified by the legislation of the Russian Federation may exercise public oversight of implementation of an initiative project in forms that do not conflict with that legislation.

local33-ufcb99efe0a825d7b29-1.text: 17. Information on the local administration’s consideration of an initiative project and on its implementation progress, including the use of funds and property and/or labor contributions by persons interested in its implementation, must be made public, including by posting it on the municipality’s official website on the Internet information and telecommunications network.

local33-u2503bfd59734949b2b-1.text: 18. The local administration’s report on the outcomes of an initiative project must be made public, including by posting it on the municipality’s official website on the Internet information and telecommunications network, within 30 calendar days after completion of the project. In a rural settlement, the rural settlement elder may bring this information to citizens’ attention.

local33-ub724b837e95d7900c5-1.text: 1. Territorial public self-government means citizens’ self-organization at their place of residence in part of a municipality’s territory to implement their own initiatives on matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life, independently and under their own responsibility.

local33-ud0e5f8d0d4272258a5-1.text: 2. The boundaries of the territory in which territorial public self-government is exercised are established by the municipal representative body on the proposal of the population residing in that territory.

local33-ubc9af2dbeb375d3cf8-1.text: 3. Territorial public self-government is exercised directly by the population through citizens’ meetings (conferences), and also through the establishment of territorial public self-government bodies.

local33-u57ab6592beb82da5ca-1.text: 4. Territorial public self-government may be exercised within the following residential territories: an apartment building, a group of residential buildings, a residential neighborhood, a rural settlement or other residential territories. Each such residential territory may belong to only one territorial public self-government organization.

local33-u847dea069e9bfaa054-1.text: 5. Territorial public self-government bodies are elected at meetings (conferences) of citizens residing in the relevant territory.

local33-ue589be7ed9a973bc9e-1.text: 6. Territorial public self-government is deemed established from the moment its charter is registered by the authorized local self-government body of the relevant municipality. The procedure for registering the charter of territorial public self-government is determined by regulatory legal acts of the municipal representative body.

local33-u6bed97bbdf95f865f9-1.text: 7. In accordance with its charter, a territorial public self-government organization may be a legal entity and is subject to state registration in the organizational and legal form of a nonprofit organization.

local33-u240e398552a891af0f-1.text: 8. A citizens’ meeting on the organization and exercise of territorial public self-government is quorate if at least one third of the residents of the relevant territory aged eighteen or over participate.

local33-u01c3fe3f03e919287e-1.text: 9. In the cases provided for by the municipal charter and/or regulatory legal acts of the municipal representative body and the charter of territorial public self-government, a citizens’ meeting’s powers may be exercised by a citizens’ conference (a meeting of delegates). The procedure for calling and holding a citizens’ conference (meeting of delegates) and electing delegates is determined by the municipal charter and/or regulatory legal acts of the municipal representative body and the charter of territorial public self-government.

local33-u8ee585671e92364acb-1.text: 10. A citizens’ conference on the organization and exercise of territorial public self-government is quorate if at least two thirds of the delegates elected at citizens’ meetings participate, representing at least one third of the residents of the relevant territory aged eighteen or over.

local33-u6c8038ec3556ad7880-1.text: 11. The exclusive powers of a citizens’ meeting or conference exercising territorial public self-government include:

local33-u652482cd5d4b85cd6d-1.text: 1) establishing the structure of territorial public self-government bodies;

local33-u26d9418c7787459432-1.text: 2) adopting the charter of territorial public self-government and amendments and additions to it;

local33-u44818a3ecd2b37004e-1.text: 4) determining the principal areas of activity of territorial public self-government;

local33-u4b49aaca1eb79bc308-1.text: 5) approving the revenue and expenditure estimate of territorial public self-government and the report on its execution;

local33-ub3da9ad504f3c151c6-1.text: 6) considering and approving reports on the activities of territorial public self-government bodies;

local33-ue8b2b08219a6a43487-1.text: 7) discussing an initiative project and deciding whether to approve it.

local33-ufa2fb8d1cf20ecb41b-1.text: 1) act in the interests of the population residing in the relevant territory;

local33-ua91bf4dba4eb9404bc-1.text: 2) may conduct economic activities for territorial improvement and upkeep and other economic activities aimed at meeting the social and everyday needs of citizens residing in the relevant territory, both using those citizens’ funds and under an agreement between territorial public self-government bodies and local self-government bodies using local budget funds;

local33-u473bb663ca22bb5a19-1.text: 3) ensure implementation of other decisions adopted at citizens’ meetings and conferences on matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life in the relevant territory;

local33-u40ffdfaff98b16ae75-1.text: 4) may submit draft municipal legal acts to local self-government bodies; these drafts must be considered by those bodies and local self-government officials competent to adopt the acts.

local33-ud48e622002e5061713-1.text: 13. Territorial public self-government bodies may propose an initiative project as project initiators.

local33-u3526b88b2604284852-1.text: 14. The charter of territorial public self-government establishes:

local33-u01557d68698bd48949-1.text: 1) the territory in which it is exercised;

local33-u7c82c983325f41f83a-1.text: 2) the goals, tasks, forms and principal areas of activity of territorial public self-government;

local33-ubade0dac7ade5f5e24-1.text: 3) the procedure for forming territorial public self-government bodies and terminating their powers, their rights and duties, and their term of office;

local33-u63ac22187b409cde45-1.text: 5) the procedure for acquiring property and for using and disposing of that property and financial resources;

local33-ue195ae9b2196e1a1fb-1.text: 6) the procedure for terminating the exercise of territorial public self-government.

local33-u650d65112608978957-1.text: 15. Local self-government bodies may not impose additional requirements on the charter of territorial public self-government.

local33-uf39bdf9bfe0793b4cd-1.text: 16. In accordance with the procedure established by a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation, territorial public self-government organizations, including those operating without registration as legal entities, may receive support from budget appropriations of the constituent entity and local budgets.

local33-uc77fb756c9b10f3f44-1.text: 17. The procedure for organizing and exercising territorial public self-government, and the conditions and procedure for allocating the necessary funds from the local budget, are determined by regulatory legal acts of the municipal representative body.

local33-u46de104c0ff34217c1-1.text: 1. To organize interaction between local self-government bodies and residents of a rural settlement when resolving matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life, a rural settlement elder may be appointed in a rural settlement located within an urban okrug or municipal okrug.

local33-ue67785490844a6efc6-1.text: 2. A rural settlement elder is appointed by the representative body of the municipality that includes the rural settlement, upon nomination by a citizens’ meeting of that settlement. The elder is appointed from among citizens of the Russian Federation residing in the settlement and having the right to vote, and citizens of the Russian Federation aged eighteen or over on the date of nomination by the citizens’ meeting who own residential premises in that settlement.

local33-u051b8ffb196c7e6025-1.text: 3. The position of rural settlement elder is not a state office, state civil service position, municipal office or municipal service position. A rural settlement elder has no employment relationship or other directly related relationship with local self-government bodies.

local33-uf58c99c0f8a0debd07-1.text: 4. A law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation may establish another title for the position of rural settlement elder, taking into account historical and other local traditions.

local33-u55d4365d252f78fa06-1.text: 5. A person may not be appointed as a rural settlement elder if the person:

local33-uebc7553d590da52bb4-1.text: 1) holds a state office or state service position;

local33-u2f33a73264557805ea-1.text: 2) has been declared legally incapable or of limited legal capacity by a court;

local33-uee175bc84f3cbbf620-1.text: 3) has a conviction that has not expired or been expunged;

local33-u37f18ee22caa6b878f-1.text: 6. A rural settlement elder’s term of office is established by the municipal charter and may not be shorter than two or longer than five years.

local33-ud0705121b14463b84b-1.text: 7. A rural settlement elder’s powers terminate early by decision of the representative body of the municipality that includes the settlement, upon a proposal of the settlement’s citizens’ meeting, and also in the cases established by points 1–7, 9 and 10 of part 1 of Article 30 of this Federal Law.

local33-ucf842a505b63487413-1.text: 8. To perform the tasks assigned to them, a rural settlement elder:

local33-u92251de23fc4e403d9-1.text: 1) interacts with local self-government bodies, municipal enterprises and institutions, and other organizations on matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life in the rural settlement;

local33-ub31bec856f9fa9ef18-1.text: 2) interacts with the population, including through participation in citizens’ assemblies and meetings, and following those events submits appeals and proposals that local self-government bodies must consider;

local33-u1b11af3ee9deec1856-1.text: 3) informs rural settlement residents about the organization and exercise of local self-government and assists in bringing other information received from local self-government bodies to their attention;

local33-u135cc454a171f85b25-1.text: 4) assists local self-government bodies in organizing and holding public hearings and public discussions and in making their results public in the rural settlement;

local33-ub1b02b119e097a3000-1.text: 5) may propose the submission of an initiative project on matters of priority importance to rural settlement residents;

local33-uda752fdd06fa6c2398-1.text: 6) exercises other powers provided for by a regulatory legal act of the municipal representative body in accordance with a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation.

local33-u906d67e7bbb95758a2-1.text: 9. Guarantees for the activities of a rural settlement elder and other matters concerning the elder’s status, including logistical and organizational support, are established by a regulatory legal act of the municipal representative body in accordance with a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation.

local33-u43ab6bc392c9e1a34f-1.text: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force
local33-u43ab6bc392c9e1a34f-1.locator: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force

local33-u66c7ae5670dc4706c6-1.text: 1. The system of municipal legal acts includes:
local33-u66c7ae5670dc4706c6-1.locator: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force

local33-ucbc7435b336f0024b1-1.text: 1) legal acts adopted at a local referendum or citizens’ assembly;
local33-ucbc7435b336f0024b1-1.locator: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force

local33-ua942e003181058fbc7-1.text: 2) legal acts of the municipal representative body;
local33-ua942e003181058fbc7-1.locator: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force

local33-u22ae56f1fd32ea030f-1.text: 3) legal acts of the head of the municipality;
local33-u22ae56f1fd32ea030f-1.locator: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force

local33-uf70cae056b9ae7ba6a-1.text: 4) legal acts of the local administration;
local33-uf70cae056b9ae7ba6a-1.locator: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force

local33-u7cf54bb6b7407f333a-1.text: 5) legal acts of other local self-government bodies and officials provided for by the municipal charter.
local33-u7cf54bb6b7407f333a-1.locator: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force

local33-u4ff14587a32295c8a4-1.text: 2. The municipal charter and decisions adopted at a local referendum or citizens’ assembly and formalized as legal acts have the highest legal force within the system of municipal legal acts, have direct effect and apply throughout the municipality.
local33-u4ff14587a32295c8a4-1.locator: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force

local33-ufd4ec6f0382c37e2c0-1.text: 3. Other municipal legal acts must not conflict with the municipal charter or legal acts adopted at a local referendum or citizens’ assembly.
local33-ufd4ec6f0382c37e2c0-1.locator: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force

local33-u713a2b7269e0d9058c-1.text: 4. The procedure for submitting draft municipal legal acts and the list and form of accompanying documents are established by a legal act of the local self-government body or official to whom the drafts are submitted for consideration.
local33-u713a2b7269e0d9058c-1.locator: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force

local33-uace5de03adba5e4646-1.text: 5. Draft municipal legal acts of municipalities containing administrative centers of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, and of other municipalities included in the relevant list by a law of the constituent entity under part 7 of this Article, that establish new or amend existing mandatory requirements for persons engaged in entrepreneurial or other economic activity, or obligations for persons engaged in investment activity, are subject to regulatory impact assessment by the local self-government bodies of those municipalities in accordance with the procedure established by municipal legal acts pursuant to a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation, except:
local33-uace5de03adba5e4646-1.locator: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force

local33-u237db29bbb4f95dd07-1.text: 1) draft regulatory legal acts of municipal representative bodies establishing, changing, suspending or abolishing local taxes and fees;
local33-u237db29bbb4f95dd07-1.locator: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force

local33-u26dfb8eda975d7fac3-1.text: 2) draft regulatory legal acts of municipal representative bodies regulating budgetary legal relations;
local33-u26dfb8eda975d7fac3-1.locator: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force

local33-u7e2beb27b83aab57a3-1.text: 3) draft regulatory legal acts developed to eliminate natural and technological emergencies for the duration of emergency regimes.
local33-u7e2beb27b83aab57a3-1.locator: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force

local33-u935c648666a3c3ac8d-1.text: 6. Regulatory impact assessment of draft municipal regulatory legal acts is conducted to identify provisions introducing or contributing to the introduction of excessive duties, prohibitions and restrictions on persons engaged in entrepreneurial and other economic activity, and provisions contributing to unjustified expenditure by such persons and local budgets.
local33-u935c648666a3c3ac8d-1.locator: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force

local33-uaae599813c7bf6997c-1.text: 7. A law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation establishes the list of municipalities in which regulatory impact assessment is mandatory for draft municipal legal acts establishing new or amending existing mandatory requirements for persons engaged in entrepreneurial and other economic activity, or obligations for persons engaged in investment activity. The law determines the criteria for including urban okrugs and municipal okrugs in that list, reflecting the objective characteristics of local self-government in that constituent entity, including the degree of concentration of state powers assigned to such municipalities.
local33-uaae599813c7bf6997c-1.locator: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force

local33-uaff59175ad5193de4b-1.text: 8. Municipal legal acts enter into force in accordance with the procedure established by the municipal charter, except regulatory legal acts of representative bodies of local self-government on taxes and fees, which enter into force in accordance with the Tax Code of the Russian Federation.
local33-uaff59175ad5193de4b-1.locator: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force

local33-u6e50949a21a1ebb52f-1.text: 9. Municipal regulatory legal acts affecting human and civil rights, freedoms and duties, municipal regulatory legal acts establishing the legal status of organizations founded by the municipality, and agreements concluded between local self-government bodies enter into force after their official publication.
local33-u6e50949a21a1ebb52f-1.locator: Article 52. System of municipal legal acts, procedure for their preparation and entry into force

local33-u3ed3725d09326bd804-1.text: Article 53. Making municipal legal acts public
local33-u3ed3725d09326bd804-1.locator: Article 53. Making municipal legal acts public

local33-uccc1c61aef4cd76d94-1.text: 1. The procedure for making municipal legal acts public, including agreements concluded between local self-government bodies, is established by the municipal charter and must enable citizens to acquaint themselves with them, except acts or individual provisions containing information whose dissemination is restricted by federal law.
local33-uccc1c61aef4cd76d94-1.locator: Article 53. Making municipal legal acts public

local33-ud206718ad4f6d05fc6-1.text: 2. Making a municipal legal act public means:
local33-ud206718ad4f6d05fc6-1.locator: Article 53. Making municipal legal acts public

local33-u3c73845ca1568354bf-1.text: 1) official publication of the municipal legal act;
local33-u3c73845ca1568354bf-1.locator: Article 53. Making municipal legal acts public

local33-u6b9f4e686070e3d077-1.text: 2) placing the municipal legal act in locations accessible to an unrestricted number of persons (premises of state bodies, local self-government bodies, state and municipal libraries, and other places open to visitors);
local33-u6b9f4e686070e3d077-1.locator: Article 53. Making municipal legal acts public

local33-u06ef1e89ef10a9e5bb-1.text: 3) posting the municipal legal act on the municipality’s official website on the Internet information and telecommunications network;
local33-u06ef1e89ef10a9e5bb-1.locator: Article 53. Making municipal legal acts public

local33-uadcaa4b3161ae97c33-1.text: 4) another means provided for by the municipal charter of enabling citizens to acquaint themselves with the municipal legal act, including an agreement concluded between local self-government bodies.
local33-uadcaa4b3161ae97c33-1.locator: Article 53. Making municipal legal acts public

local33-u836226ea9a9c059870-1.text: 3. Official publication of a municipal legal act, including an agreement concluded between local self-government bodies, means the first publication of its full text in a periodical print publication distributed in the relevant municipality, or its first posting in an online publication.
local33-u836226ea9a9c059870-1.locator: Article 53. Making municipal legal acts public

local33-ubfe71ff8990e58c11e-1.text: 4. If a municipal legal act, including an agreement concluded between local self-government bodies, is officially published in an online publication, one or more Internet access points must be established in the municipality, in accordance with Federal Law of 09.02.2009 No. 8-ФЗ “On Ensuring Access to Information on the Activities of State Bodies and Local Self-Government Bodies”, in places accessible to an unrestricted number of persons (premises of state bodies, local self-government bodies, state and municipal libraries, and other places open to visitors), without requiring those persons to use additional technical equipment.
local33-ubfe71ff8990e58c11e-1.locator: Article 53. Making municipal legal acts public

local33-uccc4b85995cd6134b7-1.text: 5. The municipal charter specifies the name of the periodical print publication and/or the name of the online publication, including the domain name of its website on the Internet information and telecommunications network and details of its registration as a mass media outlet, in which municipal legal acts, including agreements concluded between local self-government bodies, are officially published.
local33-uccc4b85995cd6134b7-1.locator: Article 53. Making municipal legal acts public

local33-ubf4a1778a79b931c56-1.text: 6. The list of periodical print publications and online publications, with the domain names of their websites on the Internet information and telecommunications network and details of their registration as mass media outlets, used to make municipal legal acts public (other than by official publication), including agreements concluded between local self-government bodies, is made generally known by publication of a legal act of the head of the municipality.
local33-ubf4a1778a79b931c56-1.locator: Article 53. Making municipal legal acts public

local33-u7db0f4ca23ef4dd252-1.text: 7. Other documents and information required by this Federal Law to be made public are made public in accordance with the procedure provided for municipal legal acts.
local33-u7db0f4ca23ef4dd252-1.locator: Article 53. Making municipal legal acts public

local33-ucdbd34c3f95b278632-1.text: Article 54. Revocation and suspension of municipal legal acts
local33-ucdbd34c3f95b278632-1.locator: Article 54. Revocation and suspension of municipal legal acts

local33-u2fc6bf1c240796c802-1.text: 1. Municipal legal acts may be revoked or suspended by the local self-government bodies or officials that adopted (issued) them; if those bodies or positions are abolished or their powers are changed, by the local self-government bodies or officials competent to adopt (issue) the corresponding act at the time of revocation or suspension; and also by a court. Insofar as an act regulates the exercise by local self-government bodies of individual state powers delegated to them by federal laws and laws of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, it may be revoked or suspended by the authorized state authority of the Russian Federation (authorized state authority of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation).
local33-u2fc6bf1c240796c802-1.locator: Article 54. Revocation and suspension of municipal legal acts

local33-ua35ba99b755f7a0acd-1.text: 2. A non-regulatory municipal legal act must be suspended immediately by the local self-government body or official that adopted (issued) it upon receipt of a corresponding order from the Commissioner under the President of the Russian Federation for the Protection of Entrepreneurs’ Rights issued under the legislation of the Russian Federation on commissioners for the protection of entrepreneurs’ rights. Local self-government bodies or officials must inform the Commissioner of compliance with the order within three days; representative bodies of local self-government must do so no later than three days after adopting their decision.
local33-ua35ba99b755f7a0acd-1.locator: Article 54. Revocation and suspension of municipal legal acts

local33-u330f8c87c50f25ecb1-1.text: 3. A court decision declaring a law of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation establishing a municipality’s status inoperative may not, before a new law of that constituent entity establishing the municipality’s status enters into force, serve as a ground for a court to declare inoperative, or for the revocation of, municipal legal acts adopted by that municipality before the court decision became legally effective.
local33-u330f8c87c50f25ecb1-1.locator: Article 54. Revocation and suspension of municipal legal acts

local33-u6b5b224a1f646534ad-1.text: Article 55. Federal register of municipal regulatory legal acts
local33-u6b5b224a1f646534ad-1.locator: Article 55. Federal register of municipal regulatory legal acts

local33-u6463144324e7497445-1.text: 1. Municipal regulatory legal acts, including decisions adopted at a local referendum or citizens’ assembly and formalized as legal acts, must be included in the constituent entity of the Russian Federation’s register of municipal regulatory legal acts. Its organization and maintenance are carried out by state authorities of the constituent entity in accordance with the procedure established by a law of that constituent entity.
local33-u6463144324e7497445-1.locator: Article 55. Federal register of municipal regulatory legal acts

local33-u5e1bd6ec2a0bd7142c-1.text: 2. The federal register of municipal regulatory legal acts consists of the registers of municipal regulatory legal acts of constituent entities of the Russian Federation.
local33-u5e1bd6ec2a0bd7142c-1.locator: Article 55. Federal register of municipal regulatory legal acts

local33-u5517bcbdf4ed0e9a1e-1.text: 3. The federal register of municipal regulatory legal acts is maintained by the authorized federal executive authority in accordance with the procedure established by the Government of the Russian Federation.
local33-u5517bcbdf4ed0e9a1e-1.locator: Article 55. Federal register of municipal regulatory legal acts

local33-u118ecefc6619f6a06b-1.text: 2) the list of powers of local self-government bodies to resolve matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life;

local33-u86552f3eaa1395eb3f-1.text: 3) the forms, procedure and guarantees for the population’s participation in resolving matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life;

local33-u8a864cb163a19bba29-1.text: 4) the structure and procedure for forming local self-government bodies;

local33-ubd7af854e71a589a26-1.text: 5) the names and powers of local self-government bodies and officials;

local33-u8fb3e54a0295158d0b-1.text: 6) the types of municipal legal acts and the procedure for their adoption (issue), public promulgation, including official publication, and entry into force;

local33-u81dfc1c2107b92f20b-1.text: 7) the types of liability of local self-government bodies and officials, grounds for that liability and the procedure for resolving the corresponding matters;

local33-ue8071f25d97d1826d1-1.text: 8) the procedure for preparing and considering the draft local budget, approving and executing the local budget, controlling its execution, and preparing and approving the report on its execution in accordance with the Budget Code of the Russian Federation;

local33-u9e850988b70b250e60-1.text: 9) the procedure for amending and supplementing the municipal charter.

local33-uda41bae6e8ba359312-1.text: 2. The municipal charter regulates other matters concerning the organization of local self-government in accordance with federal laws and laws of constituent entities of the Russian Federation.

local33-u259dbc80be7f0524fa-1.text: 3. The draft municipal charter and a draft municipal legal act amending or supplementing the charter must be officially published no later than 30 days before consideration of the adoption of the charter or amendments and additions to it, together with simultaneous official publication of the procedure established by the municipal representative body for considering proposals on the draft charter or draft municipal legal act and the procedure for citizens’ participation in its discussion.

local33-uf0df10cedb26d697f5-1.text: 4. Official publication of the procedure for considering proposals on a draft municipal legal act amending or supplementing the municipal charter and of the procedure for citizens’ participation in its discussion is not required where amendments to the charter exactly reproduce provisions of the Constitution of the Russian Federation, federal laws, or the constitution (charter) or laws of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation in order to bring the charter into conformity with those regulatory legal acts.

local33-u2ed134c8566f196ed4-1.text: 5. The municipal charter and a municipal legal act amending or supplementing it are adopted by the municipal representative body by a two-thirds majority of the established number of deputies.

local33-u594a9b700725e586d0-1.text: 6. The municipal charter and a municipal legal act amending or supplementing it are subject to state registration with the territorial body of the federal executive authority authorized in the field of registration of municipal charters, in accordance with the procedure established by federal law.

local33-ua090a8576685dd283a-1.text: 7. State registration of the municipal charter or a municipal legal act amending or supplementing it may be refused on the following grounds:

local33-uc0876d4482f194da93-1.text: 1) the charter or amending municipal legal act conflicts with the Constitution of the Russian Federation, federal laws or the constitution (charter) and laws of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation adopted in accordance with them;

local33-udfb06515e5e50833fe-1.text: 2) violation of the procedure established by this Federal Law for adopting the charter or the municipal legal act amending or supplementing it;

local33-u917e8987c245912241-1.text: 3) the presence of corruption-generating factors in the charter or the municipal legal act amending or supplementing it.

local33-uac2b28e1157330e449-1.text: 8. Refusal of state registration of a municipal charter or municipal legal act amending or supplementing it, and failure to comply with the established time limits for their state registration, may be challenged by citizens and local self-government bodies before the federal executive authority authorized in the field of registration of municipal charters and in court.

local33-u34b38929b428ea249e-1.text: 9. The municipal charter and a municipal legal act amending or supplementing it must be officially published after their state registration and enter into force after official publication.

local33-ubd1a8a6229debf9418-1.text: 10. The head of the municipality must publish the registered municipal charter or municipal legal act amending or supplementing it within seven days after receiving from the territorial body of the federal executive authority authorized in the field of registration of municipal charters the notice provided for in part 6 of Article 4 of Federal Law of 21.07.2005 No. 97-ФЗ “On State Registration of Municipal Charters”, confirming entry of information about the charter or the amending act in the state register of municipal charters of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation.

local33-u8835643c85d868b575-1.text: 11. Amendments and additions to the municipal charter changing the structure of local self-government bodies or the division of powers among them (except changes bringing the charter into conformity with federal laws, and changes to the powers, terms of office or election (appointment) procedures of persons holding municipal offices) enter into force after the expiry of the term of office of the municipal representative body that adopted the municipal legal act making those amendments and additions, except in the cases established by this Federal Law.

local33-ubbc58dad87d9b17dff-1.text: 12. Amendments and additions to the municipal charter providing for the establishment of a municipal control and accounts body enter into force in accordance with the procedure provided for in part 9 of this Article.

local33-u8c0fa8b19f42555504-1.text: 13. Amendments and additions to the municipal charter are made by a municipal legal act, which may take the form of:

local33-u608e075ae512c7ae0a-1.text: 1) a decision of the municipal representative body signed by its chair and the head of the municipality;

local33-u239b10e8a5ade1d224-1.text: 2) a separate regulatory legal act adopted by the municipal representative body and signed by the head of the municipality. In this case, the act bears the identifying particulars of the representative body’s decision adopting it. Transitional provisions and/or rules on the entry into force of amendments and additions to the municipal charter may not be included in that decision of the representative body.

local33-u67b7cdca1ed0875aad-1.text: 14. The municipal charter is brought into conformity with a federal law or a law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation within the time limit established by those legislative acts.

local33-u52e9da3bd7868e32ca-1.text: 15. If a federal law or law of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation does not establish the time limit referred to in part 14 of this Article, the period for bringing the municipal charter into conformity with that law is determined taking into account its entry-into-force date, the need to officially publish and discuss at public hearings the draft municipal legal act amending or supplementing the charter, consideration of citizens’ proposals on it, the frequency of municipal representative body meetings, and the periods for state registration and official publication of the act; as a rule, the period must not exceed six months.

local33-uf24b30257df6b7dbf8-1.text: 16. A municipal charter may not be restated in a new version by adopting a municipal legal act amending or supplementing it. In such a case, a new municipal charter is adopted, and the previously effective charter and municipal legal acts amending or supplementing it are repealed from the date the new charter enters into force.

local33-uae3a528d6816a96c03-1.text: Article 57. Decisions adopted through citizens’ direct expression of will
local33-uae3a528d6816a96c03-1.locator: Article 57. Decisions adopted through citizens’ direct expression of will

local33-u7fc6d8254f2c5d9042-1.text: 1. Citizens of the municipality directly decide matters directly ensuring the population’s daily life through the municipality’s population expressing its will directly at a local referendum or citizens’ assembly.
local33-u7fc6d8254f2c5d9042-1.locator: Article 57. Decisions adopted through citizens’ direct expression of will

local33-u70c2f6e44d04f43c44-1.text: 2. If implementation of a decision adopted through the direct expression of the will of the population of a municipality additionally requires the adoption (issuance) of a municipal legal act, the local self-government body or local self-government official whose competence includes adoption (issuance) of that act shall, within 15 days from the entry into force of the decision adopted at a referendum or citizens’ assembly, set the time limit for preparing and/or adopting the corresponding municipal legal act. That time limit may not exceed three months.
local33-u70c2f6e44d04f43c44-1.locator: Article 57. Decisions adopted through citizens’ direct expression of will

local33-ub41074a2888445688c-1.text: 3. Failure to meet the time limit for issuing a municipal legal act required to implement a decision adopted through the direct expression of the will of the population constitutes grounds for early termination of the powers of the head of the municipality, the head of the local administration or the representative body of the municipality.
local33-ub41074a2888445688c-1.locator: Article 57. Decisions adopted through citizens’ direct expression of will

local33-u69f2a6e3984c8e0443-1.text: Article 58. Rules for territorial improvement and upkeep in a municipality
local33-u69f2a6e3984c8e0443-1.locator: Article 58. Rules for territorial improvement and upkeep in a municipality

local33-uab8af0b934e3346b3f-1.text: 1. The rules for territorial improvement and upkeep in a municipality shall be approved by the representative body of the corresponding municipality.
local33-uab8af0b934e3346b3f-1.locator: Article 58. Rules for territorial improvement and upkeep in a municipality

local33-ub5611c37bedc65eaf8-1.text: 2. The rules for territorial improvement and upkeep in a municipality regulate matters concerning:
